description: An ILLUSTRATIVE instance of kye.ingest_submission.v1, showing the four states a submission moves through and what each one is allowed to claim. The operational queue is private; this example publishes the SHAPE so it is machine-readable (§43) without exposing submitter addresses or refusal reasons.

sender_policy.rule: Accepted only from an authenticated owner: the Clerk JWT with role=owner in the console, or a DMARC-passing From address on the owner allow-list by email.
sender_policy.rationale: An intake address reachable by anyone is an open write-path toward a public citation unless the sender is actually verified.

submissions.notes: Accepted and queued. NOT yet a source — nothing has been fetched, hashed, or checked for the sentence to be quoted.
The canonical acquire path fetched it, hashed it, and confirmed the quoted sentence is present. resolved_source_id being set is the proof it went through the one verifier rather than around it.

submissions.refusal_reason: HTTP 404 — the URL did not answer. A link that does not resolve is not a source, and the refusal is kept so the same one is not resubmitted next month.
submissions.notes: Refusals are retained deliberately. A deleted refusal is an invitation to try the same bad source again, having forgotten why it failed.
